A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReGuide research. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and substantial appendix additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LVLM classification and OoD-detection experiments, ReGuide evaluations, and supplementary analyses on ImageNet200 and CIFAR10.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds shared-query comparisons, a prompt-component ablation, and further error analysis.

M1.justification: The two-stage class-generation and classification procedure, suggested-class filtering, rejection class, and maximum-softmax scoring remain unchanged. The caching assumptions and prospective single-prompt implementation in Appendix C.6 do not establish a change to the evaluated method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet200 and CIFAR10 with the same constituent ID, near-OoD, and far-OoD datasets. Added shared-query comparisons, prompt ablations, and ambiguous-label examples remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator models and GPT-text remain unchanged. However, the shared-query ReGuide comparison expands from three ReGuide-equipped models in v1 Table C.2.4 to those models plus their three unmodified baselines in v2 Table C.2.2.

E3.justification: v2 adds an all-model comparison on 5,707 shared valid queries and revises the ReGuide shared-query evaluation from 2,730 queries across three augmented models to 1,430 queries across baseline and augmented configurations. It also expands FPR@90%TPR reporting and introduces prompt-ablation controls. These substantially strengthen the controlled evaluation design; the original benchmark sampling fractions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a prompt-component ablation testing guidelines and response examples (Table B.5.4), broader checks of valid-response selection effects, six additional ambiguous-label cases (Table C.3.2), and inference-cost analysis (Appendix C.6). These substantially extend the existing supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added experiments retain point estimates; the existing confidence-calibration metrics do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous reported values change. In Table 4, InternVL2-76B's baseline all-OoD FPR@95%TPR changes from 100.00 to 44.46 while its ReGuide value remains 64.36, reversing the reported direction of that effect. v2 also revises classification, calibration, and detection results elsewhere and adds shared-query, ablation, and cost results. Results on revised shared-query subsets are not directly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a limited computational-complexity derivation, including equations for baseline and two-stage inference costs under linear token/model-size scaling and cached image representations. The original problem definition and scoring equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: evaluating LVLM OoD detection and proposing model-agnostic, self-guided ReGuide to improve classification and detection. Additional evidence and revised metric-specific findings do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v1 explains high-recall failures through overconfidence, overly similar suggestions, and label noise. v2 substantially redirects the explanation toward ambiguous or inaccurate labels and superior visual recognition, explicitly asserting that the degradation is not a negative effect of ReGuide (Section 4.1 and Appendix C.3). It also adds cost-efficiency interpretations; the original limitations remain in renumbered Appendix C.7.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's hardware, software, prompts, and post-processing descriptions, v2 adds a repository link and states that sampled-image lists and per-sample prompts/responses are available. It supplies dataset/subset counts, token counts, API prices and costs, and caching/batching details. These substantially expand reproducibility and resource documentation without establishing changed implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kevin Y. Li et al.'s inference-efficiency work for cost estimation and removes Koo et al.'s Generalized Outlier Exposure citation. The positioning against CLIP-based methods, NegLabel, EOE, and prior LVLM studies remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain recognizable. Changes include localized rewriting, an expanded framework explanation, appendix subsection additions and reordering, author-order changes, and conference-header text. The document is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the conference layout, resizes and relocates existing displays, and adds a framework schematic, dataset-count tables and distribution plots, shared-query and ablation tables, an error-example table, and cost tables. ReGuide result tables gain FPR@90%TPR columns, and ROC plots are redrawn. This substantially changes visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Shared-query controls in Tables B.2.2 and C.2.2 reduce confounding from unequal valid-response sets, while the prompt ablation and expanded access/cost documentation improve empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by unexplained numerical revisions, unreconciled response counts between Tables 4 and 5, and a more categorical label-noise explanation than the case examples establish. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
